comparisons.peer_summary: The provision for credit losses increased $1.5 billion to $883 million, primarily driven by the commercial real estate office portfolio compared to a benefit in the prior year.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Bank of America disclose a reversal in the direction of their credit loss provisions in 2024 compared to prior years, though the magnitude and drivers differ. Citigroup reported a significant $126 million benefit from a net ACL release driven by changes in its margin lending portfolio. In contrast, Bank of America reported an $883 million expense (a cost, not a benefit), which was a deterioration from a benefit in the prior year, driven by the commercial real estate office portfolio.

comparisons.peer_topic: Private Banking and Lending Loan Portfolio and Credit Losses
comparisons.peer_summary: Gross loans related to Private banking and lending were $38 billion in December 2024 and $33 billion in December 2023, with average gross loans of $45.84 billion in 2024. The provision for credit losses was a net benefit of $232 million in 2024, driven by wholesale portfolio paydowns, compared to a net benefit of $508 million in 2023 which included reserve reductions related to the Marcus loan portfolio sale.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Goldman Sachs reported a net benefit (negative provision) for credit losses in 2024, indicating a release of allowances or lower than expected credit costs relative to prior periods. Citigroup's benefit was $126 million, largely due to a change in the margin lending portfolio ACL. Goldman Sachs reported a larger net benefit of $232 million for 2024, driven by paydowns in its wholesale portfolio, contrasting with its own prior year benefit which included specific reserve reductions from a portfolio sale.

sentences.text: Provisions were a benefit of $126 million, compared to a benefit of $3 million in the prior year, largely driven by a higher net ACL release.
The higher net ACL release was primarily due to a change in the ACL associated with the margin lending portfolio.
Provision for credit losses was a net benefit of $232 million for 2024, compared with a net benefit of $508 million for 2023.
The net benefit for 2024 reflected a net benefit related to the wholesale portfolio (driven by paydowns).

The net benefit for 2023 primarily reflected reserve reductions related to the sale of substantially all of the Marcus loan portfolio and lower balances in corporate loans, partially offset by impairments.

comparisons.peer_topic: Global Private Bank Expense and Credit Provision
comparisons.peer_summary: Noninterest expense was $14.4 billion, up 13%, predominantly driven by higher compensation (including revenue-related compensation and growth in private banking advisor teams) and higher distribution fees and legal expense; the provision for credit losses was a net benefit of $68 million compared to a $159 million provision in the prior year, which included a $146 million addition to the allowance for First Republic loans.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and JPMorgan Chase reported a net benefit from credit loss provisions in 2024. Citigroup reported a $126 million benefit, while JPMorgan's Global Private Bank segment reported a $68 million net benefit. This contrasts with JPMorgan's prior year, which had recorded a provision expense (cost) of $159 million due to allowances for First Republic loans, similar to how Citigroup's prior year had a much smaller $3 million benefit.
